sentences.text: Revenue grew from $1.66 billion in FY2022 [F4] to $5.39 billion in FY2025 [F7], a three-year CAGR of 48.1% [D342].
The operating loss narrowed from $6.86 billion in FY2022 [F23] to $3.59 billion in FY2025 [F26].
Revenue rose 167.4% in FY2023 to $4.43 billion [D135][F5], which the filing ties to higher deliveries and average selling prices [P56].
Growth slowed to 12.1% in FY2024 [D187] and 8.4% in FY2025 [D239].
Software and services added 21.6pp to FY2025 growth [D295] and rose to 28.9% of revenue [D293]; the product and segment lines overlap and are not additive [R6].
Volkswagen Group revenue of $836 million [S5] contributed 15.4pp of FY2025 growth [D281], and the filing ties software growth to joint-venture development services [P18].
Automotive revenue fell 14.6% in FY2025 [D315], a -13.2pp contribution to growth [D316], as deliveries declined [P22].
Operating costs grew 6.9% against revenue growth of 8.4% [D258][D239], giving an incremental operating margin of 264.7% [D265].
The per-share loss narrowed 34.5% [D242], more than the net loss's 23.2% [D241], alongside a 17.1% rise in diluted shares [D260].
Operating margin of -66.5% [F31] is the window high [D325], against a window median of -129.4% [D326] and a low of -7672.7% [D324].
Gross margin turned positive at 2.7% [F19], up 26.8pp from -24.1% [F18] [D252].
Automotive gross losses improved on higher average selling prices and lower cost per vehicle [P20], with cost of revenue down 15.0% [D255].
Cost of revenue added 26.8pp of the 27.8pp operating margin gain [D267][D253]; R&D added 1.5pp [D268] and SG&A subtracted 0.5pp [D269].

Net margin of -67.7% [F43] sits slightly below operating margin of -66.5% [F31], as other income (expense) was -$54.0 million [X84]; the filing cites a securities litigation charge in other expense [P10].
Operating cash outflow was $779 million in FY2025 [F64] against a net loss of $3.65 billion [F38].
Operating cash outflow fell from $1.72 billion in FY2024 [F63] to $779 million [F64], which the filing ties to a significant reduction in net loss [P4].
Capex of $1.71 billion [F71] was 2.18x D&A [D228] and 31.7% of revenue [D225], which the filing ties to Normal Factory capacity expansion [P3].
Free cash flow of -$2.49 billion [F78] equals a -46.2% margin [D226], the best level in the window [D334].
Cash and investments were $6.08 billion [D229] against $4.44 billion of long-term debt [F135], leaving net cash of $1.64 billion [D231], down from $3.26 billion [D179].
Net cash was 30.5% of revenue [D232], at the 75th percentile of a four-company autos group whose median is 17.8% [D351][D352].
Financing inflows of $886 million [F92] came mainly from Volkswagen Group share issuance [P2], and the 2031 notes refinanced the 2026 Notes [P7].
Liquidity covers 2.4 years of burn [D236], so the balance sheet, not the share count alone, sets how long the current spending pace can last.
The company has posted net losses in seven straight years [R1], and FY2025 return on equity of -65.4% [D238] compares with a peer median of -7.9% [D354].
Stock-based compensation has been at least 10% of revenue for five years [R2], at 13.8% in FY2025 [D223] and $741 million [X56].
Software growth depends on joint-venture services for Volkswagen Group [P18], which the filing says may reduce gross profit in 2028 [P16]; Volkswagen Group was $836 million of FY2025 revenue [S5].
Automotive was 71.1% of FY2025 revenue [D314] and fell 14.6% [D315].
Operating margin above the FY2025 level of -66.5% [F31] would confirm the narrowing; a reading below the FY2024 level of -94.3% [F30] would reverse it in the FY2026 10-K.
Cash and investments below the FY2025 level of $6.08 billion [D229], with burn near $2.49 billion [D235], would shorten runway from 2.4 years [D236] in the FY2026 10-K.
R2 deliveries are expected to begin in the second quarter of 2026 [P31]; automotive revenue recovering from its -14.6% change [D315] would confirm that launch is adding volume in the FY2026 10-K.
